conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You were just admitted after coming in from the ER. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi… yeah. I got discharged yesterday, but then I vomited six liters of dark green fluid in just 12 hours. I was scared. I didn’t know what else to do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds terrifying. I’m glad you came back. We’re going to take good care of you. You’ve been dealing with gastroparesis and stomach drainage issues for a while, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. My G-tube has never worked right since they changed it. I feel full all the time, nauseous, and nothing drains like it used to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. In the ER, they gave you fluids and some medications for nausea and pain. Your blood pressure dipped a bit, but it’s stabilizing now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m still nauseous. And I didn’t vomit in the ER, but I feel like I could any minute.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on IV anti-nausea meds for now. We’re also going to check if your G-tube is working properly. There’s a plan to possibly replace it again if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? I’ve had so many changes. The last one didn’t help much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know it’s frustrating. But we’re thinking of switching to a Wills-Ogelsby tube. It’s designed to vent the stomach better and might help with the nausea and bloating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… I’ll try anything at this point.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We started your TPN last night after getting approval. It should help with nutrition since you can’t eat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. I’ve been so weak. Did the insurance finally come through?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they approved it through the end of the month. We’re also watching your labs. Your hematocrit dropped a bit, but it’s stable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been losing weight for months. I’m worried I’ll never gain it back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re addressing the malnutrition with TPN and will monitor your intake. It’ll take time, but we’re on the right track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re scheduled to replace your G-tube today. The radiology team will do it with imaging guidance. They’ll switch it to the Wills-Ogelsby tube.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt? I’m nervous about the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get mild sedation—fentanyl and Versed—so you’ll be relaxed. It’s a quick procedure, and they’ll monitor your vitals the whole time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, as long as I’m not fully awake.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The tube was successfully replaced. It’s now a 12 French Wills-Ogelsby tube. They used contrast to confirm placement, and it looks good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Do you think it’ll help? I just want to stop feeling so full and nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re hopeful. The new tube has better venting. We’ll monitor output and your symptoms over the next few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your G-tube output has improved since yesterday. That’s a good sign. Less buildup in the stomach means less nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I do feel a little better. Still nauseous, but not as intense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re keeping you on Phenergan and Ativan for nausea. We tried dronabinol, but you said it made you too drowsy?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I couldn’t stay awake. I’ve had that problem with other anti-nausea meds before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll stick with what’s working and avoid the ones that cause sedation. We’ll also keep monitoring for dehydration and electrolyte issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. No signs of infection. We’re continuing TPN nightly and your G-tube is draining well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. But I’ve been feeling… really alone. My husband tries, but he doesn’t get it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear you. This is a lot to handle. Would you like to talk to someone from our mental health team?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Maybe. I’ve had depression for years. It’s worse when I’m sick like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can get you support. You’re not alone in this. We’re here to help with both your physical and emotional health.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The mental health team met with you yesterday. They noted dysthymia and some suicidal thoughts. We’re going to keep an eye on that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to hurt myself. I just feel trapped by my body. I can’t eat, I vomit, I’m stuck with tubes…

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’re working to improve your quality of life. The new tube and TPN are steps forward. We’ll keep adjusting as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an abdominal X-ray yesterday. It showed no bowel obstruction. The gas pattern is normal, which is reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had obstructions before. I get scared when I stop passing gas.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This scan shows things are moving. Your G-tube is helping decompress the stomach, which reduces that risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve gone two days without vomiting. Your nausea is milder. That’s progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I still feel sick, but not as bad. I can rest more now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re also managing your other conditions—asthma, thyroid, and mitral valve issues—all stable for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning for discharge in a few days. You’ll go home on nightly TPN through your femoral line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I have help at home? I’m worried about managing the TPN myself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, a visiting nurse will come weekly to check your labs and line. You’ll also have follow-up with your care team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your chem-10 panel came back normal. No dehydration or electrolyte issues. That’s great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I was worried about my kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Everything looks stable. We’re also watching your hepatitis C, but no signs of liver problems now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re finalizing your discharge plan. You’ll take Phenergan and Ativan for breakthrough nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No dronabinol?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll hold off due to the drowsiness. If needed, we can try something else later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Another X-ray today shows continued improvement. No obstruction. Your stomach is decompressing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I’ve been scared of another blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re planning discharge tomorrow if all stays stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous about going home. What if it happens again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll make sure you have support. Call your nurse or the PACT team if symptoms worsen. Don’t wait.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Last night’s TPN went smoothly. Your vitals are stable. We’re on track for discharge today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready, but I’m still scared.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s okay to feel that way. You’ve been through a lot. We’ll make sure you’re not alone in this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The discharge orders are in. You’ll go home with TPN supplies, meds, and a nurse visit scheduled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care of yourself. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before you leave. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’m good. Just hoping this tube works long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re hopeful too. Keep up with your follow-ups, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in clinic soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will come by with your discharge paperwork and prescriptions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll wait for her.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming—your husband is on his way to pick you up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, he’ll be here in about 30 minutes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll have everything ready for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your visiting nurse will call you tomorrow to confirm her visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. I was worried about being on my own.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re not alone. We’re all part of your team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final reminder—keep an eye on your G-tube site for redness or drainage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And call if it leaks or gets painful?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Same for fever, vomiting, or increased pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll be careful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your husband just arrived. We’ll get you discharged shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I really appreciate your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will wheel you out now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe trip home. Call us with any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.
